high.title: Gold prices continue sharp decline on evening 10/6
high.summary: International gold prices plummeted to $4,151/ounce on the evening of June 10, falling 2.5% from the previous close and marking the lowest level in over two months. This followed a 1.62% decline in the prior session. The sharp drop was driven by escalating Middle East tensions involving Iran that heightened inflation concerns and expectations that the US Federal Reserve will maintain its tight monetary policy stance longer. Senior analyst Lukman Otunuga from FXTM noted that while geopolitical tensions typically support safe-haven demand, gold is currently pressured by rising inflation risks. The renewed conflict between the US and Iran has diminished prospects for peace resolution while increasing global economic risks. Iran's Revolutionary Guard recently conducted missile and drone attacks on US military bases in Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain.

high.title: Dr. Dinh The Hien: Gold prices could fall to $3,500-4,000/ounce by end of 2026
high.summary: Gold markets have experienced unprecedented volatility in 2026. International gold prices surged in January 2026 to a historic peak near $5,600/ounce driven by safe-haven demand amid geopolitical tensions, central bank de-dollarization trends, and global economic concerns. Vietnamese gold prices also hit records around VND 190 million/tael. However, since late Q1, the trend reversed due to escalating Middle East conflicts, USD strength, and expectations of prolonged high Fed rates. Gold has since declined over 20% from its peak, with domestic prices falling to VND 143-144 million/tael. Dr. Dinh The Hien suggests gold could potentially fall to $3,500-4,000/ounce by year-end, marking one of the sharpest corrections in years.

high.title: State Bank approves one bank's capital increase to nearly VND 77,800 billion
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam has approved BIDV's request to increase charter capital by up to VND 4,982 billion from its capital reserve fund, bringing total charter capital to VND 77,782 billion from the current VND 72,800 billion. This follows BIDV's completion of a private placement in March that raised capital from VND 70,214 billion to VND 72,800 billion. At the annual shareholders' meeting, BIDV approved a comprehensive capital increase plan of up to VND 26,757 billion through three components: issuing shares from capital reserves (the recently approved portion), bonus shares from retained earnings, and additional private placements. This significant capital expansion strengthens BIDV's position as Vietnam's largest bank by assets and supports lending growth amid strong credit demand.

medium.title: Gold ring and bar prices evening 10/6 continue to decline
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices fell sharply by VND 5-6 million/tael on June 10, reaching the lowest levels since early February 2026. SJC gold bars traded at VND 133.3-138.3 million/tael while gold rings were at VND 133.2-138.2 million/tael. Major retailers like PNJ, DOJI, and Bao Tin Minh Chau posted similar declines of VND 5-5.5 million/tael across both buying and selling prices.

medium.title: Gold ring, gold bar prices afternoon 9/6
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices remained flat during afternoon trading on June 9 as major dealers maintained unchanged quotes from the previous session. Gold rings traded at VND 138.8-143.8 million/tael while gold bars were quoted at the same levels. International gold traded around $4,342/ounce, up 0.3% but still near yearly lows.

medium.title: Banks creating capital flows for super cities
medium.summary: Credit outstanding in Ho Chi Minh City and Dong Nai reached over VND 6.03 quadrillion by end-April 2026, up 3.84% from end-2025 and accounting for 31.1% of national credit. Credit growth focused on manufacturing (up 5.8%), agriculture (up 5.4%), wholesale/retail (up 4.4%), construction (up 3.3%) and logistics (up 3.1%), showing alignment with productive economic activities.

medium.title: Many people are getting tired of gold?
medium.summary: Despite gold prices falling sharply by VND 5.5 million/tael to VND 133.3-138.3 million/tael on June 10, there was no rush to buy gold as typically seen during price drops. Gold shops reported no queues or buying frenzy, with ample supply available and no purchase quantity restrictions unlike during the price surge period earlier this year.

medium.title: The world is waiting for a US indicator that could determine whether gold prices continue to fall or return to uptrend
medium.summary: International gold is trading around $4,200/ounce as investors await the crucial May CPI report. After months of persistent inflation keeping Fed rates high, markets are now pricing in potential rate hikes rather than cuts, which could either extend gold's decline from January's record high or spark a new rally depending on the CPI outcome.
